summary: Added a targeted DFLASH startup warning for quantized draft models, including the implicit case where draft quantization is inherited from the target. The warning calls out near-zero acceptance and the explicit unquant workaround. This mitigates the reported silent failure but does not claim to repair quantized-draft acceptance.

tests.what_was_measured: Four focused argument-resolution tests: explicit compressed-tensors warning, inherited target-quantization warning, unquantized no-warning boundary, and preservation of the explicitness provenance bit.

The complete server-argument unit module: 227 passed and 2 unrelated pre-existing context-parallel tests failed because this prepared environment is HIP and the implementation rejects prefill CP on HIP before those tests' expected assertions. Raw JUnit output is retained.
Lint invocation was unavailable because the prepared interpreter does not contain the ruff module; no lint result is claimed.

gpu_execution.evidence: The assigned GPU was identified as one AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950), but the reported acceptance collapse requires a 27B target plus draft at TP=2 on NVIDIA Marlin. Running a different single-GPU ROCm backend would not qualify that serving-path claim.

remaining_limitations: The quantized DFlash2 acceptance collapse itself remains unresolved; this change fixes the absence of a startup diagnostic only.
The reported Frozenlock 27B target weights and two-GPU TP=2 topology were not available, so no full-model acceptance-rate reproduction was claimed.
The assigned gfx950 ROCm GPU does not execute the NVIDIA Marlin path implicated by the original RTX 3090 report.

The actual syvai draft checkpoint was inspected outside JOB_WORKDIR: it declares DFlash2DraftModel with compressed-tensors W4A16 g128 and excludes candidate_selector and convolution projections from quantization.
